name: Meidan Emam, Esfahan
description: Meidan Emam is a vast public square at the heart of Esfahan, laid out in the early 1600s under Shah Abbas I. It measures about 560 by 160 metres and is ringed by two-storeyed arcades of shops. Around it stand the turquoise-domed Royal Mosque, the delicate Sheykh Lotfollah Mosque, the Ali Qapu Palace, and the gateway into the Grand Bazaar.
